# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 (Intel) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F (NetBIOS name WIRESHARKWORKSH also registered on the same host) |
| Domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (AD domain, DC at 172.16.1.4 / WIRESHARK-WS-DC) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 172.16.1.66) |
| OS (self-reported by malware) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** — a Java-based remote access trojan (RAT) known for fake-ransomware file renaming (appends `.crimson` extension) and credential/browser data theft.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The C2 beacon is unencrypted, plaintext TCP and literally names itself in every check-in packet. Reconstructed TCP stream (172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Field breakdown: `ping` (beacon type) | `STRRAT` (malware family, self-declared) | `1BE8292C` (bot/client ID) | hostname | logged-in user | OS | architecture | installed AV (Windows Defender) | STRRAT version `1.6` | victim geolocation | Java-installed flag | uptime counter. This client-ID/version format matches known STRRAT ping-beacon structure. The host queried `ip-api.com/json/` (IP geolocation lookup) immediately before the beacon session started, which is how the `US:United States` field was populated — a behavioral detail consistent with STRRAT's known geolocation lookup at startup.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — sole C2 endpoint, raw TCP, no TLS. Session ran from ~T+77s to end of capture (~508.6s duration), repeating the identical ping beacon roughly every 5 seconds.
- No DNS query in the capture resolves to 141.98.10.79 — the C2 IP appears hardcoded in the malware, contacted directly without a lookup.

**Malicious domains:** None observed. No suspicious DNS queries were made beyond legitimate Microsoft/Windows telemetry, Office, GitHub, Maven Central, and Bing/MSN infrastructure. The C2 channel bypasses DNS entirely (hardcoded IP).

**Malicious URLs:** None captured. No HTTP GET/POST to the C2 host or any other suspicious host was observed; the only HTTP requests in the capture are `GET http://www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt` (Windows NCSI check) and `GET http://ip-api.com/json/` (geolocation, sent with a spoofed Chrome 73 user-agent, itself a minor anomaly for a Windows 11 host).

**Transferred files / hashes:** None. No executable, JAR, or document was transferred over HTTP or SMB during the capture window — exported HTTP objects were only `connecttest.txt` and the ip-api JSON response; exported SMB objects were only benign Group Policy files (GptTmpl.inf, Registry.pol, gpt.ini) from the domain controller. **The initial infection/delivery mechanism (email attachment, drive-by download, etc.) is not present in this capture** — the pcap begins after STRRAT is already running and only shows post-infection C2 beaconing.

## Summary
Windows 11 host DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, user ccollier) is actively compromised with STRRAT v1.6 (bot ID 1BE8292C), beaconing every ~5 seconds to hardcoded C2 141.98.10.79:12132 in cleartext. Recommend isolating the host, resetting ccollier's credentials (STRRAT harvests browser/email credentials), and blocking 141.98.10.79 at the perimeter. No evidence of successful data exfiltration or additional payload download exists within this capture window; further analysis of endpoint artifacts (disk, memory, browser credential stores) is needed to determine delivery vector and impact.
